claim: Anthropic announced on May 14, 2026 that Claude Agent SDK, claude -p (headless), GitHub Actions, and third-party ACP apps would exit the Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise subscription usage pool on June 15, 2026, moving to a separate monthly dollar credit billed at standard API rates with no rollover.
stance_target: vendors are actively moving to meter programmatic/automated subscription usage separately from interactive usage
scope_conditions: Anthropic Claude subscriptions, announced May 14 2026, planned effective June 15 2026
quoted_support: Anthropic announced on May 14, 2026 that Claude Agent SDK and claude -p (headless) usage will exit Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise subscription pools on June 15, 2026 -- moving instead to a separate monthly dollar credit billed at standard API rates with no rollover.

claim: Anthropic confirmed via its Help Center on June 15, 2026 -- the day the Agent SDK credit change was due to take effect -- that the change was paused and is not taking effect; subscription usage continues unchanged with no new credit to claim.
stance_target: the Agent SDK credit split is currently enforced Anthropic policy
scope_conditions: Anthropic Claude subscriptions, as of June 15-16 2026
quoted_support: On June 15, 2026, Anthropic confirmed in its Help Center -- and in a note to subscribers -- that the planned move of Agent SDK, claude -p, and third-party app usage to a separate monthly credit is no longer happening.

claim: Zed Industries documented that Claude subscriptions previously subsidized heavy agent usage at roughly 15-30x compared to standalone API pricing, meaning a $20/month Pro subscriber could in theory accumulate $300-$600 in API-equivalent compute within the subscription.
stance_target: flat-rate consumer subscriptions economically subsidize heavy agentic/automated workloads relative to metered API pricing
scope_conditions: Claude Pro subscription vs. Sonnet 4.6 API pricing, as of May 2026
quoted_support: Claude subscriptions previously subsidized agent usage at roughly 15-30x compared to API pricing, and the new credits are billed at full API rates.

claim: The paused Agent SDK credit was structured as per-user and non-pooled, meaning shared CI/CD pipelines that trigger under multiple committers' credentials could not aggregate credit across a team -- Anthropic's own documentation directed such shared production automation to direct API key billing instead.
stance_target: subscription-based billing structures are not designed to support team-shared automated workloads, pushing production use toward API billing
scope_conditions: paused Anthropic Agent SDK credit proposal, May-June 2026
quoted_support: Teams running shared production automation should use Claude Platform with an API key for predictable pay-as-you-go billing.

claim: Standard-seat Enterprise plans were allocated $0 in the proposed Agent SDK credit, meaning Agent SDK workloads on those seats would have failed outright rather than metering into overage, unless upgraded to Premium seats or add-on seats.
stance_target: enterprise seat-tier structure creates hard automation-access cliffs rather than graceful metering
scope_conditions: paused Anthropic Agent SDK credit proposal, Enterprise Standard seats, 2026
quoted_support: Members of seat-based Enterprise plans on Standard seats are NOT eligible to claim the Agent SDK monthly credit. Standard Enterprise seats get $0 in new credit.

claim: OpenAI responded to Anthropic's May 14, 2026 Agent SDK credit announcement the same day by offering two free months of Codex Pro ($200/month tier) to new business customers.
stance_target: competitive dynamics between Anthropic and OpenAI on agentic subscription economics
quoted_support: Sam Altman's response was timed with precision. On May 14, 2026 -- the same day Anthropic announced the Agent SDK credit split -- OpenAI offered new business customers two months of free Codex usage.

claim: Prompt caching reduces input token cost to approximately 0.1x on cache hits, making it the single highest-leverage cost optimization for agentic workloads that repeatedly resend large system prompts or file context.
stance_target: prompt-cache optimization as a mitigation for the subscription-to-API cost gap in heavy agentic workloads
quoted_support: Prompt caching (available via the Anthropic caching docs) reduces input cost to 0.1x on cache hits -- this is the single highest-leverage optimization available.
